chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Teaching young musicians and the loss of togetherness
summary: Hinton finds young players uninterested in clarinet or academic training; Jackson says rock money and individualism replaced section playing, and togetherness in music mirrors the world.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: These musicians played great jazz and they also, Buster Bailey, a tremendous clarinet, you know, --
-- and I'm teaching now and I find out, white or black, young people aren't interested in clarinet anymore.
And the super white musician and the
super black musician, the Hubert Laws and the Frank Wess and Seldon the Selden Powell, are the ones that are playing these instruments and they're making a tremendous living.

But I find it very difficult to interest the whole complexity of young black musicians into being academic, whereas in this era you mentioned that everybody seemed to have been academic. Coleman Hawkins played piano, you played piano, organ, trombone, violin, I played violin and saxophone and bass, tuba. And I was wondering, other than what you said just now about the media, how is it that we can't seem to get these young musicians into being tremendously academic and using this for their own advantages?
Well, they see these little rock-and-roll bands making all this money.

They listen to certain things on the radio, certain types of music on the radio, you see, and you must remember that when we come up in the era of big bands you had to learn to play academically in order to play together.
Now, today, you can play solos or play anything you want to, any type of horn you can play, and it

That's right. That's right. The world is separated, Milton, if you want to know the truth, and music describes the world. There's no togetherness in the world. People don't dance together no more, They dances separately. Everybody's doing their own thing. So how are you going to have togetherness in music?
Thank you, Butter. I'm so glad --
